done_when: Pull request edits no longer delete the shared cache (changes show within its minute), forge next fetches the default branch at most once per run, and a test counts the fetches and cache refills

known.title: Queued CI failure is delivered after its rerun starts

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. While a session turn is busy, a failed workflow can enter `pending`. If that workflow is rerun before delivery, its check suite becomes queued and the current board no longer contains the completed event. This loop checks only whether the item still exists, so it delivers the old “failed” result even though the rerun is underway. The delivery test covers completed results changing, but not the interval while a rerun is queued. GitHub [documents](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/checks/suites?apiVersion=2022-11-28) that rerequesting a suite resets its status to queued and clears its conclusion.
findings.title: Queued CI failure is delivered after its rerun starts

why: Every pull request edit from any worktree deletes the shared pull request cache, and forge next fetches the default branch twice per run
